decisions.summary: T301 parts 2 to 4 (what to evict, the scratch sweep's patterns, the loose profraw files) are classed as disk work, not performance work. Disk work 'begins later' (constraint 2), 'begins after the talk on parallelizing and is ordered by time saved, never by disk freed'.
decisions.why: 462's request.md, the GM 2026-11-27: 'I would still like the disk cleanup tasks to be a higher priority than most of the rest of that new feature ... I want to make sure we get to that sooner than some of the other tasks in that feature, which are more long term in nature.' Across features, he puts orchestration first and then the disk tasks. The block cites FR-013, under which a task that is not performance work is refused at task-start while ANY open performance task exists in any active feature. Classing parts 2 to 4 as not-perf and ordering them 'by time saved, never by disk freed' therefore puts T301's disk cleanup behind the efficiency backlog's performance tasks, the reverse of the GM's order for 462. Nothing in the bundle limits the sentence to ordering disk tasks among themselves. Neither spec-cited.md nor spec-index.md carries the GM's 2026-11-27 order (spec prose outside the bundle was not seen). MODE 1 grounds: the GM's order is not impossible to follow; his words do not imply the exception, since his later 2026-11-27 words for 462 supersede the 2026-11-26 principle the sentence restates; and following his order defeats nothing. 'FR-002 says move it unchanged' is preservation, not a ground. Remedy within FR-002, leaving the moved text as it is: 462's own Summary block states that the GM's 2026-11-27 order (orchestration first, then 462's disk cleanup tasks, T301 parts 2 to 4 among them, ahead of most of the rest of 462) governs over any order a moved section states. Also, the tooling ordering FR-013 applies must let those tasks go ahead of 462's other performance tasks.

decisions.summary: T278 is a measurement only: no code changes, KEPT stays 16 and L7R_CACHE_IDLE_HOURS stays 12. Adopting the safe lever (keep 8, or keep 4 with variant_of split by unit kind) goes to a new 462 task, T556, ordered before T558.
decisions.why: Neither the GM's request nor 462's spec says how T278 must be scoped. The request moves 451's deferred work here and puts disk-cleanup work ahead of most of 462's long-term tasks. The adoption is not dropped: it is filed as T556, a disk task inside 462 at the same priority and ordered before T558, so the GM's ordering survives. The 'adopt what loses no time' order in constraint 2 comes from the task line, not from the GM's words here. Moving that work to a sibling task in the same feature does not narrow what the GM asked for. It costs one extra landing and does not defeat the purpose of the disk work.

decisions.summary: Keep 2 is ruled out because it costs 62 units and 297.9 s on the next warm build.
decisions.why: This applies the GM's rule that time saved outranks disk usage, restated in 462 T301. The cost is measured and labeled (2026-11-27, t278-runs.tsv).

decisions.summary: The idle cutoff is not a lever and stays at 12 h, because it frees 0 GB at every keep.
decisions.why: A lever that frees nothing serves no part of the disk request. The figure is measured and labeled (t278-count.tsv).

decisions.summary: variant_of's grouping of library, build-script compile and build-script run under one name is recorded as found and left; its fix goes to T556.
decisions.why: At today's keep of 16 it produces no wrong outcome: no live entry is evicted and no build loses time. Under constitution XIV it is not a defect while the keep stays at 16. It only constrains the future keep change, and T556 carries it.

decisions.summary: Method: every build runs on a scratchpad copy and live caches are read by lstat only. Units compiled, not wall time, is the cost measure, because the machine's load varied from 14 to 57.
decisions.why: This is how the measurement was done, and it serves the task's goal. Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

blocks: ### T321 (451 T104's and T304's builders each held the machine at a load of 240 to 400 for over an hour by hand on 2026-11-26, slowing two batch gates and failing a third suite; a reproduction under load had no bounded tool)

decisions.summary: COPIES copies of CMD, each LOOPS times, beside BURNERS busy loops (default 0).
decisions.why: The block cites the task line as naming copies, loops and burners. T321 moved here unchanged under FR-002, and the GM's request does not narrow its content. Offering both kinds carries the line rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: A warden in its own group plus a SIGKILL sentinel in load group G; per-run timeout rejected.
decisions.why: This is how the bound the task line asks for (MAX_MINUTES) is enforced, a design choice inside the task. Rejecting timeout is a choice of mechanism and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: One Phase line with step under-load, no category and no unit-test count, its minutes booked to tests by a new BUCKETS row; (rust,test) and src: quick rejected.
decisions.why: The task line asks for a Phase line, and the goal puts the load's minutes in make task-time. The rejected bookings would give a false count or a false source, so rejecting them serves the line.

decisions.id: D4 ahead of the run lock
decisions.summary: cli dispatches under-load ahead of the run lock so the inner make rust-test copies overlap.
decisions.why: Copies that queued behind a lock would not load the machine concurrently, which defeats the command's purpose. This is mechanism, not scope.

decisions.summary: MAX_MINUTES at most 60, COPIES+BURNERS at most 3 a core, GRACE_S 10 s, all GUESS knobs recorded in dev/audits/under-load.md.
decisions.why: Caps bound the load, which is the task's purpose. They are labeled GUESS knobs with a recorded home.

decisions.summary: Exit 1 on any red; cut runs counted apart from red; up to 10 red logs named; green logs removed.
decisions.why: The task line asks for the red count and the load at start and end. Counting cut runs apart keeps a run killed by the bound from reading as a failure of CMD.

decisions.summary: BUCKETS, its doc and bucket_of moved out of event_log_hooks.rs, re-exported, unchanged.
decisions.why: A mechanical move forced by the file-size bar (constitution X clause 13), observed by the hand-in's refusal at 1,002 lines and wc -l afterwards. No behavior changes.

decisions.summary: The 'runs ALONE in its batch' clause already stands in builder-brief.md (LOAD=1); nothing rebuilt, the Makefile help repeats it.
decisions.why: The clause the task line names exists. Rebuilding it would add nothing, so nothing is dropped.

decisions.id: D9 found-and-left: processes that leave G
decisions.summary: A CMD that starts its own process group (setsid, timeout, a cargo the pre-warm starts) leaves G and can outlive the bound; a /proc sweep was priced and not built.
decisions.why: Judged on the bundle's text alone. A non-defect left as it is counts as within, so the question is whether it is a wrong outcome (XIV v2.36.0); each escapee is judged separately. setsid in CMD is the builder's own choice to opt out of group signalling, so the bound still holds for everything the tool starts. timeout in CMD bounds itself. The pre-warm cargo is the seam, because the project's own tooling starts it: per the block it is one build that ends on its own, and it would outlive an ordinary make rust-test just the same. It is not the hour-long hand-held load at 240 to 400 that the task exists to end, so the purpose is not gutted. The block's kill measurements used CMD='sleep 60', not make rust-test, so the pre-warm tail is unmeasured. Were the canonical CMD shown to leave gate-slowing load past the bound, this would be a defect and would block. Wording only: the Caps line ('every process of a run is gone by MAX_MINUTES plus 20 s') and goal 1 ('whatever the builder does') overclaim against this bullet and should be restated as every process in G.

decisions.summary: A kill at the bound can cut a rustc mid-write, leaving one stale link that stale.rs heals once; the help says build first.
decisions.why: This is the consequence of the bound the task asks for. The block says it is healed automatically, so it is not a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: TempDir::new makes its directories under <temp dir>/l7r-tmp/ (SUBDIR) and its once-a-process sweep_dead lists that subdirectory alone, not /tmp's top level.
decisions.why: This is the task's own lever (451 T365 lever B), moved to 462 as a disk/tmp-clutter task, which the GM asked to rank ahead of most of 462 (request.md, 2026-11-27, on the order of 462's work). The three-hour and dead-pid sweep rule stays as it was.

decisions.summary: The two runners' leak checks (rustc run.rs leak_checked, hookrun.sh LEAK line) let one empty l7r-tmp through and name anything inside it as l7r-tmp/<name>. The empty directory is left in each run's TMPDIR on purpose and goes when that directory goes.
decisions.why: The leak pins keep their job: a run that leaves anything still fails, by name (pinned by l7r-tmp/l7r-leak-3). The only new pass is the empty container this task creates by design, so nothing the leak checks were meant to catch is excused.

decisions.summary: Found beside the task: tree::command_head no longer cuts a walk target's head at 120 characters, so builder_pool_hooks and parked::shell_hits refuse a long command they already refuse when it is short. The context-cap band's message still cuts its own copy at 120.
decisions.why: This fixes a defect found during the task: a guard passed bad work (a pool tree could be removed by hand, or a parked stage moved, by any command over 120 characters). The standing fix-as-we-go rule (constitution XIV) covers it. It adds no new rule, only the same rule at any length. The search space for the other readers of the cut text is stated (grep over rust/ for .head and .segment), and each hit is accounted for.

decisions.summary: builder_brief's block-length test now counts the block with the fixture's directory read as /diagram/.clones, because the fixture path (about 91 characters) pushed the block to 2,024 against its 2,000 cap, while a real pool tree's path is about 37 characters. The code that writes a real brief is unchanged.
decisions.why: The test still enforces the 2,000 cap on a block as a real pool tree would render it. Only the fixture's artificial path length is taken out, so this is not a check loosened on real work. Lengths are observed, with the method stated.

decisions.summary: Helper-form directories already at /tmp's top level are no longer swept by any TempDir. One empty directory was measured. It is left, not filed, for T374's wider /tmp rule.
decisions.why: The measured residue is one empty directory (observed 2026-11-27, ls -A /tmp filtered to the helper form). New code makes no more of them, so the residue cannot grow, and no reader sees it and no finding breaks. That makes it a difference, not a defect (XIV, GM 2026-11-19), and leaving a non-defect as it is stays within what was asked. The disk-cleanup purpose is not gutted, because the task removes the top-level listing and leaves nothing that grows.

decisions.summary: T377, T378 and T379 are left open. Withdrawing T377 and T378 is for the session once this lands, and T379 waits on T372.
decisions.why: The task withdraws nothing and changes no other task's scope. It only records how those tasks' own conditions read after it lands.

decisions.summary: T371 runs after T370 and before T377/T378, independent of T372, as a [perf] task under 451 FR-013 (performance first).
decisions.why: Ordering inside the backlog, consistent with FR-013 and with the GM's ranking of disk work ahead of most of 462 (and behind orchestration where builders can be kept busy with it). No requested work is dropped.
